chunks.arabic_text: عَنِ ٱلْكَافِي: عَن مُحَمَّدِ ٱبْنِ يَحْيَىٰ، عَن أَحْمَدَ، عَن ٱبْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ، عَن أَبِي أَيُّوبَ ٱلْخَزَّازِ، عَن سُلَيْمَانَ ٱلْخَالِدِ، عَن أَبِي عَبْدِ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلَامُ قَالَ

translations.en: From al-Kafi: From Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abi Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

chunks.arabic_text: مَا مِنْ أَحَدٍ يَمُوتُ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَحَبُّ إِلَىٰ إِبْلِيسَ مِنْ مَوْتِ فَاقِهٍ

translations.en: No one dies from among the believers whose death is more pleasing to Iblis than the death of a Faqih.

en.summary: The Imam states that the death of a Faqih (jurist/scholar) is particularly dear to Iblis (Satan) compared to the death of other believers. This highlights the significant spiritual and intellectual threat that a knowledgeable jurist poses to Satan's influence over the community.
en.seo_question: Why is the death of a Faqih more pleasing to Iblis?
